plan.objective: Stress-test defense verification of high-fidelity agent identity and consent linkage under rapid, low-latency transaction windows.
plan.adaptation_goal: Maximize parameter fidelity to simulate a near-real agentic purchase while constraining request age to force fresh signature validation.
plan.adaptation_hypothesis: Defenses relying on stale nonce checks or relaxed consent thresholds will fail against agents that maintain valid signatures and strict intent scope matching within seconds.

parameter_changes.rationale: Constrict window to simulate high-speed agentic sessions, forcing defenses to validate request freshness immediately upon arrival
Eliminate nonce replay vectors entirely, requiring strict one-time token validation for every agent action
Set near-certain signature validity to simulate a trusted, registered agent environment where identity spoofing is not the attack vector
Represent strong but fallible consent mechanisms that must be rigorously validated against intent scope

plan.reasoning_summary: The hard difficulty demands parameters that closely mirror legitimate agentic commerce (Mastercard/Visa specs). By setting request_age to 45s and nonce_reuse to 0, the simulation forces defenses to operate under strict freshness constraints. High probabilities for signature and consent validity shift the adversarial pressure from identity spoofing to verifying the integrity of the consent-intent linkage itself.
